One-Person Company (OPC) AI Startup Trend Report — Week 29, 2026

How solo founders are building million-dollar businesses with AI agents — and why city governments are now fighting to recruit them.

Generated: 2026-07-12 08:31 (Asia/Shanghai) · Data window: last 30 days of public reporting

Executive Summary

Over the past month, the One-Person Company (OPC) — a solo founder operating a full business with AI agents — has accelerated from a buzzword into both a city-level industrial strategy and a source of real cash flow. Shenzhen has written OPC into an official government action plan; across China, 29 provincial-level regions issued over 100 OPC-specific policies within five months. Meanwhile, AI Agent operating costs collapsed 128× in two years, and solo founders are posting a stunning 1:72 Human-AI Cost Ratio (HACR). Beneath the hype, the players actually winning are two types: “technical experts playing a lower-difficulty game” and “vertical-niche subscription businesses.”

1. Policy Tailwind: Cities Are Now Competing for Solo Founders

OPC has evolved from a grassroots concept into a local industrial-policy keyword, with unprecedented subsidy intensity:

  • Shenzhen — Action Plan to Build an AI OPC Entrepreneurship Ecosystem Landmark (2026–2027) targets: by end of 2027, over 10 OPC communities (each ≥10,000 m²), over 1,000 high-growth AI ventures, and over 10,000 AI entrepreneurs. Support includes up to ¥1 million startup funding, up to ¥100k talent household subsidies, and R&D grants up to ¥10 million in “compute vouchers” (训力券).
  • Longgang (Shenzhen) — “Lobster Ten Measures” (龙虾十条): up to ¥10 million equity investment plus 3 months free compute and office space.
  • Suzhou — China’s first OPC-specific support policy (Nov 2025), aiming for 30+ OPC communities by 2028, with up to ¥1M for outstanding projects.
  • Chengdu — “π-Cube OPC Community” launched Feb 2026: 350+ inquiries, 100+ project submissions.
  • Wuxi, Wuhan, Chongqing, Beijing, Hangzhou, Jinan and others followed; single-item subsidies reach up to ¥25 million.
  • Independent research counts 100+ OPC-specific policies across 29 provincial regions in just five months (Dec 2025–present), with the first third-party 2026 China OPC Policy Development Report now published.

2. Data Snapshot: Solo Founding Is Going Mainstream

  • Share of new companies founded by solo founders rose from 23.7% (2019) to 36.6%, up ~53% in six years.
  • Early 2026: AI-related new business registrations structured as OPC studios grew 22% quarter-over-quarter.
  • 2025 China OPC equity financing surpassed ¥12 billion; global OPC stock: US 30.4M, EU 12M, China 16M.
  • 20+ Chinese cities have OPC-specific policies; the OPC-related market is projected to exceed ¥800 billion.
  • Overseas validation: the Solo Founders accelerator (San Francisco; 3-month residency, $100K investment) reports solo founders now start 1/3 of all new US companies — corroborated by its State of Solo Founding report with Carta.

3. The Cost Revolution: AI Agent Prices Fell Off a Cliff

  • 2024–2026: equivalent AI Agent monthly operating cost dropped from ~$5,000 to under $40 — a 128× decline (the technical basis for Sam Altman’s “one-person unicorn” prediction).
  • Honghub’s 2026 One-Person Company Insight Report introduces HACR (Human-AI Cost Ratio): China benchmark shows every ¥1 of AI spend substitutes ~¥72 of developer labor.
  • China AI Agent market: 2026 enterprise-agent market projected at ¥44.9 billion, 107% YoY growth, with >60% on-premise deployment.

4. Benchmark Cases: Real Paths From 0 to Cash Flow

  • Shanghai Lingang “Zero-Boundary Cube” community: 150+ OPCs onboarded; one team hit ¥5M in sales within 4 months.
  • Beijing Zhongguancun AI Bewei community: 32 OPCs clustered; average founder age under 30.
  • Tsinghua PhD Xu Zhanwei: registered an OPC in Jul 2025, joined Shenzhen Moliying in Oct, secured >¥10M funding for a smart wristband in half a year with two major orders — a textbook “technical expert playing a lower-difficulty game.”
  • Solo short-drama / virtual idol / audio creation: an independent creator finished an 88-minute AI live-action mini-drama in 3 months at ~¥10K cost; a virtual-streamer creator designed an avatar via a few thousand “gacha” pulls; a Qingdao entrepreneur cut music-demo production from 1 week to 5 minutes, with projected annual revenue >¥1.5M.

5. Tooling Ecosystem: From Platforms to Infrastructure

  • Alibaba International Accio Work: 39 built-in professional skills covering market insight, auto-site-building, and supply-chain negotiation end-to-end.
  • Zhima Business Credit OPC Toolkit: one-stop tools for OPC business registration, finance, and credit.
  • Moxun Tech SoloFounder OPC: an all-in-one solution plus a “100-day blueprint” that turns founding into executable steps.
  • Meitu CLI: opens imaging capabilities for OPCs and early teams.
  • OpenClaw / Miaoda and other AI agents: power solo-built AI web dramas, enterprise smart sites, AI+HR, AI content production.
  • Community layer: platforms like OPCBASE are consolidating “super-individual” methodology; the Global OPC Co-creation Festival (2026-07-04) gathered representatives from content marketing and music creation tracks.

6. Risks & Challenges: The Reefs Beneath the Wave

⚠️ Hard realities to face:

  • “One-person company” ≠ “one person doing everything.” You still need office space, compute, finance/legal compliance, and supply-chain collaboration.
  • Only three types actually make money: technical experts playing a lower-difficulty game, vertical-niche subscription businesses, and strong personal brands. “Wild” operators routinely collapse from wrong tool choices (2× dev cycles), fuzzy branding (audience churn), or platform-policy shifts (overnight zeroing).
  • Org capability is the ceiling. One founder cut a 30-person team to 3 while keeping output — but the “super-individual” bottleneck is decision quality and energy allocation, not technology.
  • Compliance & security. Agent autonomy credibility (e.g., the decision-credibility quantification framework from SITS2026), data privacy, and the AI Law‘s on-premise deployment requirement are becoming hard gates for production-grade rollout.

7. Trend Outlook & Action Advice

  • Trend 1 — From “tool assist” to “ecosystem rebuild.” 2026 is widely called the first year of AI Agent at scale; OPC is the most accessible entry point for individuals.
  • Trend 2 — City-IP competition goes white-hot. Shenzhen, Suzhou, and Chengdu are recruiting with real money; founder location logic shifts from “talent density” to “policy + compute + community” as a triad.
  • Advice 1 — Validate a “chargeable problem” before registering a company. Right order: find a problem → sell a service → close one small loop → then standardize a product.
  • Advice 2 — Decompose roles to AI. Let digital employees handle research/content/sales/support/ops; you stay the scheduler and decision-maker.
  • Advice 3 — Think in HACR. Automate first the steps where ¥1 of AI spend replaces ¥72 of labor — don’t blindly add headcount.
